acceptedWorkingLayout: 13 columns, case examples first, CSAPI adjacent to far-right proposed DIM

reviewedExistingCells.edition: OGC 23-001, Part 1: Feature Resources, v1.0.0, published 2025-07-16
reviewedExistingCells.originalStandardMeaning: System instances can link via systemKind to a Procedure describing the kind/model (e.g. datasheet); a link is not the model string itself.
reviewedExistingCells.nonEquivalenceCaution: A model is reusable; a System remains an instance. Keep model ID separate from physical serial and API URL.

reviewedExistingCells.edition: OGC 23-001, Part 1: Feature Resources, v1.0.0, published 2025-07-16
reviewedExistingCells.originalStandardMeaning: System uniqueIdentifier is a required persistent identifier independent of its canonical /systems/{id} URL.
reviewedExistingCells.nonEquivalenceCaution: A persistent System ID is not necessarily the manufactured item's physical serial.

reviewedExistingCells.edition: OGC 23-001, Part 1: Feature Resources, v1.0.0, published 2025-07-16
reviewedExistingCells.originalStandardMeaning: System is a feature representing an individual sensor, actuator, platform, process or other connected system as typed by systemType and optional assetType.
reviewedExistingCells.nonEquivalenceCaution: A focal reference arrangement, a manufactured assembly, a physical constituent, and a whole deployed station need not share one System identity.

reviewedExistingCells.edition: OGC 23-001, Part 1: Feature Resources, v1.0.0, published 2025-07-16
reviewedExistingCells.originalStandardMeaning: System subsystems are regular System resources nested under parents; source explains composition versus aggregation and permits separately deployed interchangeable payloads.
reviewedExistingCells.nonEquivalenceCaution: A linked System or nested resource does not, by itself, prove a physical constituent, manufactured chip, permanently installed part or inspected cable.

reviewedExistingCells.edition: OGC 23-001, Part 1: Feature Resources, v1.0.0, published 2025-07-16
reviewedExistingCells.originalStandardMeaning: A Deployment associates deployed Systems with an optional platform feature; platform can be a System or another Feature. System can carry a Platform semantic type.
reviewedExistingCells.nonEquivalenceCaution: Deployment location, station/site context, and the actual individual probe position are distinct; platform need not be a System.

reviewedExistingCells.edition: OGC 23-001, Part 1: Feature Resources, v1.0.0, published 2025-07-16
reviewedExistingCells.originalStandardMeaning: Procedure resources can describe an observing method or a reusable equipment type; implementing a Procedure is distinct from actually performing an Observation.
reviewedExistingCells.nonEquivalenceCaution: The Procedure resource can be a method OR datasheet kind; do not collapse executed behavior or processing implementation into a type link.

reviewedExistingCells.edition: OGC 23-002, Part 2: Dynamic Data, v1.0.0, published 2025-07-16
reviewedExistingCells.originalStandardMeaning: Per-DataStream observation schema and resultSchema encode result fields and types by observation format. These are information structures, not transducer hardware addresses.
reviewedExistingCells.nonEquivalenceCaution: A named result field is not automatically a physical transducer channel or IEEE 1451 channel.

reviewedExistingCells.edition: OGC 23-002, Part 2: Dynamic Data, v1.0.0, published 2025-07-16
reviewedExistingCells.originalStandardMeaning: DataStream observedProperties identifies the measured property semantics; Part 1 Property definitions also distinguish observed, controlled and asserted properties.
reviewedExistingCells.nonEquivalenceCaution: A property URI is not a reported field name, raw output channel, physical sensor module or evidence of an actual measurement.

reviewedExistingCells.edition: OGC 23-002, Part 2: Dynamic Data, v1.0.0, published 2025-07-16
reviewedExistingCells.originalStandardMeaning: The DataStream system association identifies the producer for the stream; observations in that stream are produced by the same System.
reviewedExistingCells.nonEquivalenceCaution: The stream-producing System may be a station/logger/process; the physically sensing contributor and original event issuer require independent evidence.

reviewedExistingCells.edition: OGC 23-002, Part 2: Dynamic Data, v1.0.0, published 2025-07-16
reviewedExistingCells.originalStandardMeaning: An Observation resource is associated with a DataStream and includes phenomenonTime, resultTime and result; the structure supports multiple observed properties.
reviewedExistingCells.nonEquivalenceCaution: A valid API Observation representation does not authenticate a manufacturer example or prove a new original measurement event.

reviewedExistingCells.edition: OGC 23-002, Part 2: Dynamic Data, v1.0.0, published 2025-07-16
reviewedExistingCells.originalStandardMeaning: A Command is associated with a ControlStream; parameters represent desired controlled values with issueTime/currentStatus on server-reported Commands.
reviewedExistingCells.nonEquivalenceCaution: Published syntax, available command definitions, or manufacturer request flags are not evidence an actual Command was issued.

reviewedExistingCells.edition: OGC 23-002, Part 2: Dynamic Data, v1.0.0, published 2025-07-16
reviewedExistingCells.originalStandardMeaning: CommandStatus carries dated progress reports and enumerated codes such as ACCEPTED, EXECUTING, COMPLETED and FAILED.
reviewedExistingCells.nonEquivalenceCaution: ACCEPTED is not execution success; a reported COMPLETED status should not be treated as independently measured physical effect.

nativeSourceFactsHeld.caution: A time-bounded deployment can associate a System with a platform. It is a candidate carrier for installed/service roles, not evidence of a particular Bennett's Point probe join or exact swap minute.
Part replacement is an event category, but a generic event record does not by itself specify full old/new serial IDs or the exact time of the Bennett EE181 change.
Station point or deployment area does not become the individually surveyed position of every probe.
Diagnostic/status datastreams are conceptually supported, but no actual Campbell Status event from an installed station has been obtained.
A dated change event does not furnish full previous/next configuration values or prove present effective settings.
Property definitions can distinguish an hourly mean from basic temperature, but do not prove the processing method executed or the source-to-result causal chain.
These temporal properties are required in CSAPI representation; historical source data may not furnish original resultTime, so do not invent it.
A declared live control channel and status vocabulary are not proof of authenticated command execution or observed physical effect.
